text: In the 1960s, the sugar industry quietly hired Harvard scientists.
Their job? Review what really causes heart disease.
Early studies were starting to point at sugar. The industry was worried.
So it picked the question, and mailed over the studies it wanted challenged.
One scientist wrote back: "We are well aware of your particular interest."
The review ran in a top medical journal. Sugar? Played down. Fat? The main target.
Nobody told readers who paid for it.
Fifty years later, in 2016, researchers found the letters in old archives.
And the price of that review? Just six thousand five hundred dollars.
No one proved the money changed a word. But the science had a sponsor, and nobody was told.
